evidence_basis: Chang J-Y, Chang N-S 2015, Oncotarget 6(6):3578-89, PMCID PMC4414138. ADVERSARIAL RE-READ of a paper first read on 2026-09-20 under FTR-20260920-25650666-01. The prior read established what the paper claims; this one asks whether the claims are carried by the experiments, because this paper is the SOLE SOURCE of the first mechanistic node of the entire Chang/NCKU neuro-proteostatic cascade and of the discovery lead DL-BIO-004.

VERDICT: SINGLE-LAB, UNCORROBORATED, AND IT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE LOAD-BEARING STEP. Verified personally against the artefact: the Discussion's own summary states 'We determined that TGF-beta1 causes dissociation of WWOX from TPC6ADelta, thus leading to the aggregation of TPC6ADelta and TIAF1 and subsequent events including activation of caspases, and Abeta production' - while the SAME Discussion states 'Whether TGF-beta1 regulates the binding of WWOX with TPC6ADelta is unknown and is being determined in this laboratory.' THE STRINGS immunoprecipit / co-IP / pull-down OCCUR ZERO TIMES IN THE WHOLE ARTEFACT (these are roman-type method words, not italicised tokens, so this count is informative). There is no binding assay in the paper. The WWOX-to-TPC6ADelta physical link, on which the node depends, is asserted in the abstract and in the Discussion summary and disclaimed as unknown two paragraphs later.

THE ISOFORM'S SPLICING ORIGIN IS PREDICTED, NOT OBSERVED. Verbatim: 'Results from 2 different web-based tools (NNSplice and NetGene) all predicted that the nt position 85 can be used as an alternative 5' donor site to initiate splicing and leads to a 42-bp deletion on exon 1 sequence.' The protein is 'deduced'. No junction-spanning RT-PCR, no splice-junction sequencing, no mass spectrometry anywhere. What IS clean: genomic PCR plus sequencing on 30 human samples showing the 42 bp is not a genomic deletion.

ANTIBODY VALIDATION IS PEPTIDE COMPETITION ONLY. Verbatim Methods: 'Specificity of the antisera was tested using the synthetic peptides to block immunostaining.' No knockout, no knockdown, no full-length-only background - although the lab uses a TPC6Asi siRNA construct ELSEWHERE IN THIS SAME PAPER and never applies it as an antibody control. This is a NEO-JUNCTION polyclonal, the antibody design that most requires a genetic null before it can be believed.

THE HUMAN POST-MORTEM ARM IS A NULL REPORTED AS A TEMPORAL ORDERING, AND IT IS AGE-CONFOUNDED BY ~21 YEARS. Figure 3 legend, verbatim: 'No significant difference was shown in TPC6A or TIAF1 aggregation for samples between younger nondemented controls (14 samples per group; total 3 groups; 42 to 76 years old) and older AD patients (24 samples per group; total 4 groups; 71 to 90 years old).' Controls 59 +/- 17 years, AD 80 +/- 8.8 - diagnosis and age are perfectly confounded for EVERY between-group claim in this arm. The abstract renders this as 'aggregate formation of TPC6ADelta occurs preceding Abeta generation in the hippocampi of middle-aged postmortem normal humans' - a temporal claim from a cross-sectional null over two non-overlapping age bands in which nobody was measured twice. No blinding, no PMI, no sex, no Braak stage, no scoring rule, no multiple-comparison correction.

THE FILTER RETARDATION ASSAY IS ISOFORM-BLIND, so the abstract's attribution of it to the isoform is an inversion. Verbatim: 'Both wild type TPC6A and TPC6ADelta are present in the aggregates, as determined using the TPC6A (84-100) peptide antibody.' And the quantity the abstract implies is discriminating is not: 'TPC6A aggregates were found in both control and AD groups to a similar extent (~40% positive), suggesting that TPC6A aggregates are relatively stable in the brain.'

THE ~40% p-WWOX REDUCTION EXISTS AND IS CORRECTLY RECORDED IN DL-BIO-004, BUT IT INHERITS THE AGE CONFOUND AND IS SELF-CITED. Verbatim: 'In agreement with our previous reports, the levels of protein aggregates for Tyr33-phosphorylated WWOX (p-WWOX) were significantly reduced by ~40% in the AD samples, compared to nondemented controls.' Same cohort, same 21-year age gap, same unblinded dot blots - so the contrast is as consistent with ageing as with diagnosis, and its only corroboration is the same laboratory's earlier work.

WWOX DEPENDENCE DOES NOT CLASSIFY AS ONE THING, AND SPLITTING IT IS THE USEFUL RESULT. FORMATION of the isoform: WWOX-INDEPENDENT AS MEASURED - WWOX is never manipulated in any splicing experiment and the isoform was cloned from WWOX-competent U937 cells. POLYMERISATION: WWOX-INHIBITORY - this is the paper's real finding, 'When WWOX was knocked down by siRNA (WOX1si), ectopic TPC6ADelta and TIAF1 became aggregated by greater than 80% of cells (~100 cells counted)', versus under 10% with WWOX present. TOXICITY (caspase 3, Abeta): WWOX-INDEPENDENT-DOWNSTREAM - all of it in SK-N-SH cells with normal endogenous WWOX. In vivo arm: UNCLEAR, no wild-type comparison is reported for the isoform.

EVERY CAUSAL RESULT IS ECTOPIC OVEREXPRESSION OF A FLUORESCENT FUSION; every endogenous result is descriptive. The strongest arm (aggregation on WWOX knockdown) is ectopic, in COS7 MONKEY KIDNEY FIBROBLASTS, at 24 h, scored manually over ~100 cells, with no knockdown-efficiency quantification and no WWOX re-expression rescue. Two limits the authors state themselves: dosing is 10 micrograms of construct to reach 50-75% apoptosis, and 'Transiently overexpressed wild type TPC6A or TPC6ADelta was equally potent in causing cell death' - so the ISOFORM-SPECIFIC toxicity claim survives only on the narrower caspase-3 readout.

THE MOST DISEASE-RELEVANT ENDOGENOUS LOSS-OF-FUNCTION STATEMENT IN THE PAPER CARRIES NO FIGURE. Verbatim Discussion: 'We found that knockout MEF cells are prone to possess aggregates of TPC6A, TIAF1, JNK1 and upregulated expression of beta-secretase and Tau tangles (data not shown)'. DATA NOT SHOWN is where the WWOX-null-to-aggregation link actually lives.

DIRECTION FOR A LOSS-OF-FUNCTION GENOTYPE: ADVERSE. Less WWOX means more aggregation - 'suggesting that without WWOX, TPC6A and TIAF1 start to polymerize or aggregate' - and the authors' own proposed mechanism is explicitly speculative: 'The likely scenario is that WWOX may act as a chaperone, which stabilizes proteins from misfolding and being degraded by the ubiquitin/proteasome system.' Four caveats travel with it: the MEF result is data not shown; the mouse is a complete null dying at about one month, so a dying-animal confound is unaddressed; the frame is Alzheimer's rather than DEE; and this paper's human WWOX measurement is of aggregated Tyr33-phospho WWOX, not total protein, in the age-confounded comparison.

NODE COLLAPSE - TPC6ADelta AND TIAF1 ARE NOT TWO CORROBORATING NODES, THEY ARE ONE OBSERVATION. Same laboratory, same tissue bank ('Human postmortem frozen hippocampal tissues were obtained from the Department of Pathology, University of Colorado Health Sciences Center (by Dr. CI Sze, before 2005). IRB approval was waived.'), probed on the same filter-retardation membranes, same overexpression figure, same unvalidated antibody practice, and 'Similar results were observed with TIAF1 aggregates.' Counting them separately DOUBLE-COUNTS ONE MEASUREMENT. Corroboration weight for the pair is ONE, not two.

D-15, AND THE DISTORTION IS THE VERB, NOT THE ADJECTIVE. The attributed phrase is NOT in the body at all. THE CHAPTER'S FRAMING QUESTION WAS RE-ISSUED AS ITS ANSWER.

NAMED FAILURE MODE, NEW TO THIS REPOSITORY: INTERROGATIVE-TO-DECLARATIVE RE-VOICING. A source's question is quoted accurately and re-attributed as its finding. It leaves NO LEXICAL FINGERPRINT - every content word matches - so quote-matching and string comparison cannot catch it. Only reading the sentence's GRAMMATICAL MOOD catches it. This is a distinct class from the abstract-versus-results inversions recorded seven times in this literature, which are contradictions between two parts of one paper rather than a change of mood on the way out.

THE SENSORS PROPOSAL IS EXPLICITLY SPECULATIVE, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO IN THE SAME SENTENCE. The only common shared aspect by all these mechanisms is that they can eventually lead to a MECHANICAL BREAKAGE of CFSs.' So it reviews both sides on mechanism and proposes - without claiming to have shown - that the CONSEQUENCES are not merely structural. It leans; it does not settle.

FLUX WAS MEASURED, BUT IN THE WRONG ARM AND IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY. A citation reading 'WWOX acts on autophagy THROUGH mTOR' would overread this paper.

On the paper's own endpoint that is survival-promoting, which the authors treat as BAD BECAUSE THEY WANT THE CELL TO DIE: 'A clear strategy in cancer targeting is boosting WWOX for suppression of autophagy in treating cancers.' The paper measures nothing about whether elevated autophagy in a WWOX-scarce non-cancer cell is protective, neutral or harmful, and makes no extrapolation outside oncology.

ABSTRACT VERSUS RESULTS: THREE OVERSTATEMENTS AND ONE REVERSE OMISSION, NO INVERSION. (b) The abstract claims WWOX regulates susceptibility 'in vitro and CURE of SCC in MTX therapy'; the paper's own data are immunohistochemistry and TUNEL on biopsies and the cure is attributed in the body to PREVIOUS studies - no survival data, no response rate, no n, no control arm. (d) REVERSE OMISSION, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: THE KNOCKOUT-MEF RESULT IS ABSENT FROM THE ABSTRACT ENTIRELY. The single most transferable datum in the paper is invisible to an abstract-only reader, WHICH IS WHY THE REGISTRY STUB COULD NOT HAVE BEEN CORRECTED WITHOUT THE FULL TEXT.

VERDICT: PARTIAL. The paper ESTABLISHES that one missense WWOX allele (P252A) is lost POST-TRANSCRIPTIONALLY by a LYSOSOME-DEPENDENT, PROTEASOME-INDEPENDENT, MACROAUTOPHAGY-INDEPENDENT route, that the mutant protein binds HSC70, and that the step is pharmacologically blockable at a protein-abundance readout. SECOND INSTANCE IN ONE DAY OF THE RE-VOICING FAILURE MODE, AND THE SOURCE'S OWN WORD IS 'SPECULATED'. Results, verbatim: 'Since the KFERQ-like motif (LRSVQ at 187-191 amino acids) exists on WWOX, WE SPECULATED that lysosomal degradation of WWOXmutant protein occurred through chaperone-mediated autophagy.' The abstract and the closing Discussion paragraph state the same thing as demonstrated: 'undergoes accelerated degradation VIA chaperone-mediated autophagy in the lysosome, directly linking protein instability to loss-of-function.' ANYONE QUOTING THE ABSTRACT IMPORTS A HYPOTHESIS AS A FINDING - which is exactly what the census that surfaced this paper did, and what the interrogative-to-declarative rule recorded earlier today exists to catch.

WHAT THE DEGRADATION EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS. PRESENT: qRT-PCR showing mutant mRNA is not decreased, so the loss is post-transcriptional; cycloheximide chase (50 ug/mL, 0-10 h); MG-132 NEGATIVE - 'We found that the proteasome inhibitor, MG-132 treatment, did not induce the accumulation of WWOX ... proteins' - excluding the proteasome; 3-MA negative, excluding macroautophagy; chloroquine and NH4Cl positive; a CQ+CHX combination; K63-linked polyubiquitin typing with a K63R control; LAMP1 immunofluorescence co-localisation; and an HSC70 co-immunoprecipitation that is mutant-positive and wild-type-negative. ABSENT: any LAMP2A manipulation, bafilomycin, HSC70 knockdown, KFERQ mutagenesis, isolated-lysosome uptake, a CMA reporter, and ANY HALF-LIFE VALUE.

THE RESCUE IS REAL BUT NARROW, AND NOTHING FUNCTIONAL WAS MEASURED UNDER IT. Chloroquine 40 uM 24 h and NH4Cl 250 uM 24 h restore P252A protein level in CAL-62 cells STABLY OVEREXPRESSING A FLAG-TAGGED CONSTRUCT, read out by western blot band intensity. Two non-selective lysosomotropic agents, one thyroid-cancer line, one transgene. No chemical chaperone, no HSC70 or LAMP2A modulator, no proteostasis drug, and NO FUNCTIONAL ASSAY IS RUN UNDER RESCUE - not colony formation, invasion, comet, gammaH2AX or NHEJ. THE ROUTE IS BLOCKABLE; WHETHER BLOCKING IT RESTORES ANYTHING IS UNTESTED.

THE SINGLE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DATUM FOR THIS DISEASE MODEL POINTS AGAINST A SIMPLE READING, AND IT IS A HUMAN ONE. Verbatim Discussion: 'In this study, the cancer patient harboring germline homozygous P252A and P282A variants DID NOT SUFFER FROM WWOX-RELATED NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASE.' The proband was a 35-year-old man, homozygous for two missense substitutions that are INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM EMPTY VECTOR across colony formation, viability, Matrigel invasion, wound healing, xenograft volume and weight, comet, gammaH2AX and an I-SceI/EJ2GFP NHEJ reporter. CANCER-ASSAY-DEAD IS NOT NEUROLOGICALLY NULL. The authors' own reading is the one this repository should carry: 'However, WWOX and WWOX mutants MAY HAVE SOME RESIDUAL PROTEIN FUNCTION to maintain the development of the neurological system.'

DOMAIN PLACEMENT IS NOT THE PAPER'S AND MUST NOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO IT. The variants are c.754C>G p.(Pro252Ala) in exon 7 and c.844C>G p.(Pro282Ala) in exon 8, germline HOMOZYGOUS - not compound heterozygous - confirmed by Sanger in adjacent normal muscle, with an unaffected heterozygous son and a wild-type wife; P282A is the known SNP rs3764340. Both residues fall within the SDR/ADH span by external coordinates, WHICH IS THE READER'S ARITHMETIC: 'SDR', 'ADH' and 'short-chain' occur ZERO times in the body (roman-type, informative). The domain schematic is a figure and per D-14 was not inspected.

ONLY ONE OF THE TWO ALLELES IS THE DEGRADED ONE, AND THE OTHER IS THE CLEANER EXPERIMENT. P252A loses abundance; P282A loses function WITH NO STABILITY DEFECT. For P252A abundance and function are CONFOUNDED AND NEVER SEPARATED - the paper itself invokes low abundance to explain the lost POLE4 co-IP ('likely due to the low abundance of the unstable WWOXmutant') and then asserts causality for tumour suppression with 'directly correlated'.

THREE FURTHER ABSTRACT-STRONGER DIVERGENCES. The abstract claims 'complete loss of tumor-suppressive activity' where the Discussion allows residual function; it says POLE4 interacts with wild-type 'but not' the mutant where the Results say it 'appeared to' lose the interaction AND NO NUCLEOTIDE-EXCISION-REPAIR ASSAY EXISTS ('the functional relevance of WWOX-POLE4 interaction in nucleotide excision repair remains to be elucidated'); and it says germline LOF variants 'drive' cancer pathogenesis where the Discussion says 'probably predisposing'. Internally, Results say the mutant 'was transferred' to lysosomes while the figure legend says it 'has a trend to be' transferred.

NO NEURAL OR DEVELOPMENTAL ENDPOINT EXISTS: 'seizure' occurs ZERO times (roman-type). DO NOT CITE THIS PAPER FOR ANY WOREE, SCAR12 OR SEIZURE ENDPOINT. The clinical genetics is n = 1 proband; all functional work is engineered overexpression in CAL-62, BCPAP and HEK293T plus CAL-62 nude-mouse xenografts, with no knock-in and no patient-derived line. Rigour: 'blind' and 'random' occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative); n = 3, mean +/- SEM, repeated uncorrected two-tailed t-tests.

WHAT THIS REPOSITORY MAY TAKE FROM IT - ONE MECHANISM CLASS AND ONE DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION, NOT A CONCLUSION. For any SDR-domain missense WWOX allele the question to ask is: IS THE PROTEIN PRESENT AT NORMAL ABUNDANCE, OR IS IT BEING DEGRADED DESPITE NORMAL mRNA? Those are different molecular diseases with different intervention points, and this paper demonstrates the second is real for a WWOX SDR missense substitution. RECORD THE ROUTE AS lysosome-dependent, proteasome-independent, macroautophagy-independent degradation with an HSC70 co-IP and a PREDICTED KFERQ-like motif - NOT as chaperone-mediated autophagy.

THE PAPER MAKES NO CLAIM THAT PHENOTYPE PREDICTS GENOTYPE CLASS, and it imports the opposite: 'A recent review DID NOT HIGHLIGHT A CLEAR CORRELATION between the extension of [WWOX] mutation and the onset or severity of epilepsy.' SO IT DOES NOT CONTRADICT OLIVER 2023 - if anything it weakly corroborates it. The title's 'phenotypic-driven approach' is a narrative diagnostic heuristic for recognising THE DISEASE, never an algorithm for inferring THE ALLELE CLASS, and the paper subordinates it explicitly: 'Yet, genetics is pivotal to making the definitive diagnosis and for parental counseling.' No claim needs re-opening on this basis.

THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT IS THERAPEUTIC, AND IT IS A COMPLETE FOUR-WAY NEGATIVE IN ONE BIALLELIC-NULL PATIENT. Verbatim: 'Several anti-seizure medications (ASM) were ineffective (i.e., valproate, VIGABATRIN, clonazepam, clobazam, levetiracetam, rufinamide, and CBD OIL) or determined adverse events such as extreme drowsiness or increased secretions (i.e., phenobarbital, nitrazepam). Moreover, THREE CYCLES OF ACTH HAD VERY POOR RESULTS. THE KETOGENIC DIET DID NOT SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE SEIZURES AND WAS SUSPENDED.' THIS CLOSES A GAP DL-MECH-022 NAMED EXPLICITLY - that the null literature had never tested vigabatrin, ACTH, cannabidiol or the ketogenic diet. All four have now been tried in one patient and all four failed. NOTE ON NAMING: the literal string cannabidiol occurs zero times because the paper writes 'CBD oil' - that zero is a NAMING DIFFERENCE, NOT A NEGATIVE.

AN UNEXPLAINED INTERNAL TENSION, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: vigabatrin is listed among the ineffective drugs and is nonetheless RETAINED in the current regimen at 70 mg/kg/day. The paper does not explain it.

AND THIS IS NOT A WEST-SYNDROME CASE, WHICH BOUNDS THE COMPARISON: hypsarrhythmia, burst, spasms and 'West syndrome' all occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). So it is not comparable to vigabatrin-responsive infantile spasms in other reports. Seizure onset was DAY ONE OF LIFE - 'A few hours after birth, he presented hypoglycemia, respiratory distress associated to tonic-clonic seizures' - against a stated WOREE mean of 2-3 months, making this the extreme early tail; then multi-daily asymmetric tonic seizures up to 50 a day that 'never responded to any pharmacological treatment'. Reported, never recommended; nothing here is medical advice.

RED FLAG AGAINST A HYPOTHESIS THIS SESSION WAS BUILDING, AND IT IS IN PROSE, SO D-14 DOES NOT SHIELD IT. THE CEREBELLUM IS ABNORMAL IN THIS PATIENT FROM DAY 7. Results: 'Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies performed at the age of 7 days and 2 months showed frontal bilateral periventricular cysts, enlargement of cerebral subarachnoid spaces ... and A SMALL INFERIOR VERMIS.' At 2 years 4 months: 'MILD SIGNAL ALTERATIONS WERE ALSO NOTED AT THE LEVEL OF THE PONS AND DENTATE NUCLEI.' Discussion: 'our patient showed mild progressive brain atrophy, delayed myelination, and INFERIOR CEREBELLAR VERMIS HYPOPLASIA.' AND AT LITERATURE LEVEL: 'structural brain abnormalities including corpus callosum hypoplasia, progressive cerebral atrophy, CEREBELLAR VERMIS HYPOPLASIA, and white matter hyperintensity ... HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED IN MOST CASES.'

BUT THE TWO PROPOSITIONS ARE NOT THE SAME PROPOSITION, AND MUST NOT BE SCORED AGAINST EACH OTHER AS IF THEY WERE. Midline VERMIAN HYPOPLASIA ON MRI in a human infant is a developmental-volume statement about the midline. CLAIM 039's finding is that the rat lde/lde CEREBELLUM SHOWS NO MARKED PATHOLOGICAL ALTERATION ON HISTOLOGY while ataxia is 95% penetrant. A hypoplastic vermis and an unremarkable cerebellar cortex on light microscopy can both be true. WHAT DOES FALL IS THE GENERAL READING - 'the cerebellum is spared in WWOX-DEE' is NOT supportable, and the acquisition note written earlier today around PMID 26345274 is corrected in the same cycle.

THALAMUS: thalam* occurs ZERO times (roman-type, informative) - no thalamic involvement in this patient, which is worth recording because PMID 26345274's abstract reports selective mediodorsal thalamic degeneration in one of its five patients.

THE INDEX PATIENT LACKS THE CARDINAL LITERATURE FEATURE AND THE PAPER DOES NOT ADDRESS IT: microcephal* occurs three times, NONE of them about this patient; the only head-circumference values are 50th centile at birth and 25th at 4 months. A paper proposing phenotype-first recognition whose own index case lacks the cardinal feature is worth noting as a limit on the heuristic.

GENOTYPE IS NULL/NULL, SO THERE IS NO MISSENSE OR SPLICE DATA HERE: acceptor and donor occur ZERO times (roman-type); splice occurs once as a variant-filtering term; SDR once as generic protein description. Do not cite this paper for an SDR-domain missense or splice-acceptor question.

A METHODOLOGICAL LESSON WITH CONSEQUENCES FOR EVERY ALLELE-CLASS CENSUS: 'Exome Sequencing detected the stop variant c.790C>T (p.Arg264*) in one allele ... No other potentially pathogenic variants were identified in the exome. CNVS ANALYSIS WAS ALSO UNREMARKABLE.' The second allele - an 84,828 bp deletion removing exon 6 - was found only by Q-PCR and confirmed by array-CGH. A PATHOGENIC SINGLE-EXON WWOX DELETION WAS INVISIBLE TO EXOME CNV CALLING AT AN EXPERT CENTRE, SO ALLELE-CLASS CENSUSES BUILT FROM NGS-DIAGNOSED PATIENTS ARE LOWER BOUNDS FOR INTRAGENIC CNVs.

ABSTRACT VERSUS RESULTS: ONE REAL DISCREPANCY, ONE HEDGE RUNNING THE UNUSUAL DIRECTION, ONE FRAMING EFFECT, NO INVERSION. (1) ASSAY MISATTRIBUTION: the abstract credits the transcript-level exon 5-7 fusion to Q-PCR, the DNA dosage assay; the Results attribute the fusion product to RT-PCR and the exon-6 dosage result to Q-PCR. An attribution error, not a strength error. (2) The body is HARDER than the abstract - abstract 'usually leads to severe disability OR death', Introduction 'leading to severe disability AND death' - the inverse of the standard failure mode recorded seven times in this literature. (3) Title and abstract are more supportive of phenotype-first diagnosis than the body is, and the material that would let a reader evaluate it lives only in the Discussion. (4) Every numerical and genetic result was checked one by one and matches.

PATIENT ALIVE AT ABOUT 4 YEARS (figure legend), gastrostomy at 3 years; died, survival and autopsy occur ZERO times, so there is no survival endpoint here. No developmental milestones were achieved; ophthalmological examination and auditory brainstem response were both normal, which is an ABSENT ophthalmological involvement in a biallelic-null patient.

evidence_basis: You Y et al. 2024, Mol Genet Genomic Med 12(8):e2500, PMCID PMC11298992. Read as the ONLY REACHABLE member of a bounded census asking a question this repository had never answered: HAS ANYONE MEASURED WHAT A WWOX SPLICE ALLELE ACTUALLY PRODUCES? DL-BIO-002 and TX-001 were both in-silico only (SpliceAI / Pangolin), and TX-001 is a splice-correcting ASO whose efficacy endpoint is the fraction of correctly spliced transcript.

CENSUS CORRECTION, FILED AGAINST THE BRIEF THAT COMMISSIONED THIS READ. The task was written on the premise that this repository had never read a paper measuring a WWOX splice allele's transcript. THAT PREMISE WAS WRONG for this paper: it is already PAPER 016, carrying a legacy_reconstruction (FTR-20260726-39101447-01) whose registry record declares 'full text reviewed (PMC open access)' - but with a coverage map that is unknown_legacy throughout and no fingerprinted artefact. So this event is the FIRST CONTEMPORANEOUS receipt over a fingerprinted artefact, superseding that reconstruction, not a first contact with the paper. The census's finding about the FIELD stands unchanged; its statement about this REPOSITORY did not, and is corrected here rather than in the analysis alone.

CENSUS RESULT, WHICH IS ITSELF THE FINDING: of 20 splice-relevant records, THREE measured a transcript from a cis splice-affecting WWOX allele and TWO merely ANNOTATED one - six patients across two canonical alleles whose RNA was never examined. Only ONE of the three is reachable here. All four splice-allele measurements are from groups OUTSIDE the Chang/NCKU laboratory (Hebei, Tsukuba, Israel, Melbourne); exactly one census record is inside it and it concerns TRAPPC6A splicing, not WWOX.

VERDICT ON THE PAPER: MEASURED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THIN. The allele is c.172+1G>C, homozygous through uniparental disomy of chromosome 16 - and it is a canonical DONOR, not an acceptor, so it is one class removed from the reference genotype's allele. The assay is a MINIGENE, NOT PATIENT RNA: exons 1-3 with an ARTIFICIALLY SHORTENED INTRON 1, transfected into HEK293T, RT-PCR plus Sanger. Patient blood yielded DNA only.

WHAT THE ALLELE PRODUCED - EXON SKIPPING. Verbatim from the figure legend, which survived extraction more cleanly than the body: 'the c.172+1G>C substitution of WWOX caused a splicing abnormality, which abrogated the intron 2 canonical splice site and led to a LOSS OF EXON2.' No intron retention and no cryptic site are reported - but neither is excluded in prose, and A TWO-EXON MINIGENE WITH A TRUNCATED INTRON IS A POOR INSTRUMENT FOR DETECTING EITHER.

NO NMD BLOCK ANYWHERE, AND THE ASSAY IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO NMD IN ANY CASE. Verified personally: cycloheximide, emetine, actinomycin and 'nonsense-mediated' all occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). A truncated construct has no downstream junction to trigger surveillance. SO THE DEGRADED-VERSUS-STABLE FRACTION IS UNKNOWN.

PROTEIN WAS NOT MEASURED - IT WAS TRANSLATED IN SOFTWARE. Methods, verbatim: 'Finally, Snapgene software was used to translate nucleotide sequences into protein sequences, and the influence of variation on the protein translation process was analyzed.' 'western' and 'immunoblot' occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). YET THE PAPER STATES: 'A minigene assay used to confirm the variation site revealed that the variation RESULTED IN PROTEIN TRUNCATION.' A MINIGENE ASSAY CANNOT REVEAL PROTEIN TRUNCATION.

NO QUANTIFICATION OF ANY KIND. 'densitomet*' occurs ZERO times (roman-type). The entire quantitative content of the splicing result is: 'The gel-electrophoresis of RT-PCR revealed a band for wild-type and another for mutant-type.' A qualitative gel plus Sanger.

NO RESCUE OR CORRECTION ARM. 'antisense' and 'oligonucleotide' occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). The only restoration language in the paper is a citation to third-party rodent Wwox re-expression work.

ABSTRACT VERSUS RESULTS: DIVERGENCE PRESENT, AND IT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE TODAY OF SPECULATION RE-VOICED AS FINDING. 'Affected splicing' is earned. 'Causing protein truncation' is an IN-SILICO translation voiced as an assay result. 'And affecting its function' has NO FUNCTIONAL ASSAY OF ANY KIND behind it. And the therapeutic sentence is a MOOD UPGRADE: the Discussion hedges correctly - 'levetiracetam, phenobarbital, and topiramate effectively controlled early seizures, while vigabatrin treatment decreased epileptic seizures, SUGGESTING THAT VIGABATRIN MAY BE an effective management option' - while the abstract drops the hedge, on an n-of-1 under three concurrent anti-seizure medications. NOTHING HERE IS MEDICAL ADVICE AND NO TREATMENT INFERENCE IS DRAWN.

WHAT DL-BIO-002 AND TX-001 MAY NOW ASSUME: a canonical WWOX splice allele has been shown, by direct sequencing of its spliced product, to cause EXON SKIPPING - and across all four census measurements EVERY reported product is an exon skip, with no intron retention and no cryptic site reported by anyone. A canonical ACCEPTOR allele has been measured once (c.517-2A>G giving skipping of exon 6, PMID 30853297), the closest published analogue to the reference genotype's class - but that is an ABSTRACT SENTENCE ON AN UNREACHABLE PAPER: reported-measured-but-unread, census and not evidence.

WHAT REMAINS UNMEASURED, AND THE LARGEST HOLE IS THE THERAPEUTIC ONE. No WWOX splice allele has EVER been assayed with an NMD inhibitor, so the degraded-versus-stable fraction is unknown for every allele. NO ABERRANT-TO-NORMAL RATIO EXISTS ANYWHERE, IN ANY WWOX ALLELE, IN ANY TISSUE - SO TX-001'S EFFICACY ENDPOINT HAS NO MEASURED BASELINE DENOMINATOR. No protein has ever been observed from a WWOX splice allele. NO ASO OR SPLICE-CORRECTION ARM EXISTS IN THE WWOX LITERATURE AT ALL, so TX-001 has zero in-gene precedent. And the reference genotype's own allele was measured by nobody.

TRACTABLE LEAD, RECORDED AS A LEAD AND NOT A PLAN: the Genoa group of PMID 35573960 already holds WOREE patient fibroblasts and runs WWOX RT-PCR, while TEN PATIENTS ACROSS TWO CANONICAL ALLELES - a 2026 Argentine founder cohort (c.107+1G>A, five patients, PMID 42721537) and the 2015 c.606-1G>A cohort (PMID 26345274, five patients) - have never had their RNA examined. One cheap experiment, patient fibroblast RT-PCR across the junction plus or minus cycloheximide with band quantification, would convert DL-BIO-002 from in-silico to measured AND supply TX-001's missing denominator.

INSTRUMENT STATE, WITH A USEFUL POSITIVE: the italic-deletion defect is ACTIVE - 'thegene' occurs NINE times where the italic gene symbol was deleted between 'the' and 'gene', and bare WWOX survives only nine times, so that count is an instrument reading. BUT HGVS TOKENS SURVIVED IN THE BODY (c.172+1G>C appears eleven times intact) WHILE FAILING IN THE TITLE, which is corrupted to 'c.172+>C' - so body HGVS counts are usable and title ones are not. Two near-miss false positives were caught and corrected in the audit: case-insensitive 'ASO' matches ultrasound and basolateral, and 'NMD' matches NMDAR; both true counts are zero.

DECLARED LIMIT: no figure image is inspectable in this environment and none was inspected. The splicing result's gel is a figure; per D-14 nothing is adjudicated from it beyond the prose and legend text quoted above.

evidence_basis: Park YH, Hodges A, Simmons A, Lovestone S, Weiner MW, Kim S, Saykin AJ, Nho K 2020, Neurol Genet 6(6):e517, PMCID PMC7577551. THIS IS FT-098, THE SECOND OF THE THREE 'INDEPENDENT COHORT' LEGS behind a Wave 2 claim that the GENE TRAPPC6A has independent human-genetic support for a neurocognitive role - a claim already RETRACTED IN FULL after leg 1 read null on replication and leg 3 failed the authors' own permutation. Read to discharge the debt, not to reopen the claim.

THE LICENCE-WALL CLASSIFICATION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. This leg was recorded as 'licence-walled, unread, counts in neither direction' on the strength of get_copyright_status returning is_open_access false - with checked_sources ['pubmed'], meaning PMC WAS NEVER QUERIED. A single fetch returned a complete body: Introduction through Conclusion, Methods, Results, Discussion and limitations. STANDING RULE FROM THIS: never record 'licence-walled' from a copyright status whose checked_sources omits pmc without first attempting get_full_text_article.

VERDICT: IT CAN BEAR ON THE NODE-INDEPENDENCE QUESTION, AND IT BEARS AGAINST IT. This is a BLOOD TRANSCRIPTOMIC CASE-CONTROL study that runs NO GENETIC ASSOCIATION TEST OF ITS OWN; its headline result is a SIX-GENE COMPOSITE SCORE; and its only neurocognitive statement about the gene is an EXTERNAL CITATION. FT-098 was never independent support, and reading it does not make it so.

THE GENE IS READABLE - NOT BY SYMBOL BUT BY ITS HGNC APPROVED NAME IN ROMAN TYPE. Discussion, verbatim: 'encodes trafficking protein particle complex 6A.' and 'Although it is not clear how it affects the pathogenesis of AD, genetic variation of[it] is reported to be associated with nonverbal reasoning.' No reconstruction was needed. Verified personally: the italic symbol TRAPPC6A occurs ZERO times in the body, and THE PUBMED METADATA ABSTRACT DOES NOT RESCUE IT EITHER - it is damaged identically ('andwere significantly upregulated, andwas significantly downregulated'). WHICH OF THE SIX RESULTS SLOTS THE GENE OCCUPIES IS NOT READABLE ON THIS SURFACE and was not reconstructed by position, ordering or plausibility.

NO SINGLE GENE IS LOAD-BEARING - ONLY THE COMPOSITE, AND THE SCORE ERASES COMPONENT IDENTITY BY CONSTRUCTION. Methods, verbatim: 'we polarized gene expression levels by changing the sign of the expression levels for genes labeled as low expression. Thus, ELEVATED RISK FROM GENE EXPRESSION, IRRESPECTIVE OF THE DIRECTION OF RISK, could be additively incorporated in the TRS.' The per-gene test that exists is explicitly a CHECK THAT THE SELECTION STEP BEHAVED, not an independent association test, and HALF THE TARGET GENES FAILED IT IN ADNI: 'Expression levels of the remaining 3 genes in ADNI were not significantly different.' No per-gene effect size or p-value appears in the main text and no multiple-testing correction is stated for those six tests. MEMBERSHIP IN A SIX-GENE POLARISED SCORE IS NOT PER-GENE HUMAN-GENETIC EVIDENCE FOR THAT GENE.

EFFECT SIZES ARE SMALL AND ONE IMAGING ENDPOINT FAILS TO REPLICATE. ADNI discovery, 103 AD versus 213 controls: OR 1.18 (95% CI 1.07-1.31) for COLOC and OR 1.18 (1.06-1.33) for SMR; WITHOUT the colocalisation step only OR 1.06 (1.01-1.13). AddNeuroMed replication: OR 1.20 (1.12-1.30) and OR 1.23 (1.13-1.35). But: 'There was no significant association between the TRS and the hippocampal volume in AddNeuroMed.' Bonferroni is stated for GENE SELECTION ONLY; no correction is stated for the per-gene or score-versus-biomarker regressions; covariates are age and sex plus intracranial volume, field strength and education; APOE is genotyped but is NOT a covariate.
THE JOURNAL RATES IT CLASS III AND SAYS WHY: 'The study is rated Class III because of the case control design and the risk of spectrum bias.'

GENE-LEVEL THROUGHOUT, FROM THE METHODS, SO IT HAS NO PURCHASE ON THE ISOFORM. Affymetrix U219 and Illumina HT-12 v3 expression arrays, gene-level eQTL input, and an explicit collapse: 'if a gene contained more than 1 microarray probe, we selected only the probe with the greatest variance.' The roman-type words isoform, splice and exon occur ZERO times (informative). NOTHING HERE CAN DISTINGUISH TRAPPC6A-DELTA FROM FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT.

ABSTRACT VERSUS RESULTS: NO SOFTENING, OMISSION OR INVERSION OF SUBSTANCE - THE ABSTRACT IS ACCURATE, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING after seven papers in this literature where it was not. The one asymmetry is that the failed hippocampal replication is handled by omission from the replication sentence rather than by statement; the body states the null plainly.

AND THE MOOD CHECK INVERTS THIS SESSION'S FAILURE MODE ONTO US. The authors wrote 'genetic variation of[it] IS REPORTED TO BE associated with nonverbal reasoning' - passive, cited, not measured - immediately after conceding 'it is not clear how it affects the pathogenesis of AD', and closed with 'Our findings thus represent ASSOCIATION NOT CAUSALITY.' Every mechanistic statement in the paper is marked as modal. THE SOURCE DID NOT OVERSTATE. THE WAVE 2 READING RE-VOICED THE SOURCE'S CITATION AS THE SOURCE'S FINDING. That is the fourth instance of interrogative-or-cited-to-declarative re-voicing recorded today, and the cleanest, because here the error is entirely ours.

A STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION STRONGER THAN THE RETRACTION NEEDED, RECORDED AS PROBABLE AND UNVERIFIED: the phenotype this paper cites for the gene - NONVERBAL REASONING - is leg 3's phenotype (PMID 21766012). The superscript reference number was destroyed by the extractor, so THE CITATION TARGET COULD NOT BE CONFIRMED ON THIS SURFACE. If it holds, LEGS 2 AND 3 ARE NOT INDEPENDENT OF EACH OTHER, and the three-cohort claim was never three cohorts.

EXTRACTION DEFECT, PRESENT AND SEVERE: every italicised gene symbol is deleted, with the collision 'includingand' proving silent unmarked deletion; all p-value exponents are destroyed and NONE WAS RECONSTRUCTED; tables, figure legends and references are absent, and the per-gene statistics live in a supplementary table that is not present. The HGNC expanded names are roman type and survive, which is what made the gene identifiable at all - a technique worth reusing on this surface.
DECLARED LIMIT: no figure image is inspectable in this environment and none was inspected. Per D-14 nothing asserted only by a panel is adjudicated.

RECORD FOR FT-098: move from 'licence-walled, unread' to OPEN ON THE PMC ROUTE, READ, EXTRACTION DEFECT DECLARED. It is NOT independent support for the TRAPPC6A node. THE RETRACTION IS NOT REOPENED: the debt is discharged, the claim is not revived.

evidence_basis: Baryla I, Styczen-Binkowska E, Pluciennik E, Kosla K, Bednarek AK 2022, Int J Mol Sci 23(6):3326, PMCID PMC8955937, CC BY 4.0. Medical University of Lodz - INDEPENDENT OF BOTH Chang/NCKU and Aqeilan/HUJI, established from affiliations rather than surname counts. This was one of only TWO remaining UNREAD_PREMISE entries in the whole repository; the reasoning layer has leaned on it since before the current discipline existed.

TWO REGISTRY GLOSS ERRORS, AND THE SECOND IS THE SAME AMPUTATION FOUND EARLIER TODAY ON CORPUS-STUB-139. The metabolism meta-file holds this as 'Paper 64 - WWOX/HIF1A axis downregulation -> altered glucose metabolism'. (a) IT IS PRIMARY EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH, NOT A REVIEW - article_types carries no Review tag - and the repository had been treating it as one. (b) THE GLOSS IS UNSCOPED: the result exists only in ONE IMMORTALISED HUMAN SKIN FIBROBLAST LINE (1BR.3.N, ECACC 90020508) under four defined oxygen/glucose conditions, AND THE CONDITIONS ARE EXACTLY WHERE THE DIRECTION REVERSES.

IT IS A KNOCKDOWN, NOT A KNOCKOUT, THOUGH THE PAPER CALLS IT 'KO' THROUGHOUT: CRISPR/Cas9 sgRNA with puromycin selection, polyclonal, and section 2.1 reports mRNA only about 3-fold lower. Every claim inheriting the word 'knockout' from this paper inherits a partial depletion.

THE DISCUSSION CONTRADICTS ITS OWN RESULTS ON THE LOAD-BEARING STEP, AND I VERIFIED BOTH SENTENCES PERSONALLY. Discussion: 'We determined that knock-out of[WWOX] leads to increased[HIF1A] mRNA and protein level TOGETHER WITH ITS TRANSLOCATION TO THE NUCLEUS and raise of its transactivation function.' Results 2.6.1: 'the expression of HIF1alpha protein was SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED in 1BR.3.N KO ... in cytoplasm fraction' and 'We didn't observed WWOX influence on HIF1alpha protein in NUCLEAR FRACTION.' THE BLOT WAS POSITIONED TO DETECT TRANSLOCATION AND DID NOT DETECT IT. What survives is the HRE-transactivation reporter, which is the paper's robust positive; the protein-level and nuclear-translocation claims do not.

DIRECTION IS WEAKER AND LESS CONSISTENT THAN THE ARC ASSUMES. Lactate is the ONLY readout consistent across all four conditions. GLUCOSE UPTAKE REVERSES SIGN: 'silencing significantly INCREASED glucose uptake in normoxia normoglycemia and REDUCED glucose uptake in hypoxia hyperglycemia'. And THE OXIDATIVE ARM WAS MEASURED AND WAS NULL: 'citrate synthase expression and activity were tested and we did not observe WWOX influence on it', with PDH activity unchanged in all four conditions. No Seahorse, no OCR, no ECAR (roman-type zeros). So the 'away from OXPHOS' half of the Warburg framing rests, in human cells, ON PDK TRANSCRIPT ALONE.
NOTHING NEURAL AND NOTHING DEVELOPMENTAL. Verified personally: brain, neuron, epilep*, seizure all occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). The system is a skin fibroblast line.

NO METABOLIC INTERVENTION IS PROPOSED OR EVALUATED: ketogenic, dichloroacetate and metformin all occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). The only therapeutic language targets WWOX itself in diabetes - 'strategies to normalize glucose metabolism by targeting[WWOX] may have promise as therapies in the future' - not the metabolism and not the brain.

EXTRACTION DEFECT: all italicised tokens deleted including the italic p of p-values, leaving '(< 0.05)'; 125 emptied citation markers; THE REFERENCE LIST DID NOT SURVIVE, so no citation target was resolved and none was reconstructed. PubMed's own title string for this PMID is itself corrupted by italic deletion ('TheAxis Downregulation'), so the defect is in the metadata record and not only in the extractor.
DECLARED LIMIT: no figure image is inspectable here and none was inspected; per D-14 every quantitative claim above is taken only from prose carrying its own numbers.

evidence_basis: Baryla I, Kosla K, Bednarek AK 2022, 'WWOX and metabolic regulation in normal and pathological conditions', J Mol Med (Berl) 100(12):1691-1702, PMCID PMC9691486. article_types carries Review. Medical University of Lodz - independent of Chang/NCKU and Aqeilan/HUJI. Registry gloss ('review: WWOX e metabolic regulation, comprehensive') is ACCURATE. The LAST of the repository's two UNREAD_PREMISE entries.

VERDICT ON THE ARC: THE FIELD'S OWN SYNTHESIS DOES NOT SUPPORT A METABOLIC INTERVENTION IN A WWOX-LOSS GENOTYPE AT BETTER THAN HYPOTHESIS STRENGTH. The arc is real but is measured in fibroblasts, muscle, liver, flies and cancer lines; NEVER in neural tissue and never in a developmental setting.

IT PROPAGATES THE CONTRADICTED CLAIM RATHER THAN THE MEASURED ONE, AND IT IS THE SAME GROUP SEVEN MONTHS LATER. Verbatim: 'Our further analysis ... in a human fibroblast cell line revealed that ... deficiency leads to increased[HIF1A] mRNA and protein expression. ADDITIONALLY, IT INCREASES THE TRANSLOCATION OF HIF1A TO THE NUCLEUS and amplifies its transactivation function.' The primary being cited is PMID 35328751, whose Results say the nuclear fraction showed NO WWOX influence and whose cytoplasmic HIF1alpha protein DECREASED. THIS IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE TODAY OF A SOURCE'S UNSUPPORTED SENTENCE BEING RE-VOICED AS ESTABLISHED - and the worst shape of it: a laboratory citing its own paper's Discussion over its own paper's Results.

ITS ONLY DIRECTIONAL STATEMENT ABOUT BRAIN METABOLISM RUNS AGAINST A KETOGENIC RATIONALE: 'It has been shown that INCREASING GLYCOLYSIS MAY SLOW NEURODEGENERATION.' A ketogenic rationale in this model is built on shifting AWAY from glycolysis. The review does not notice the tension because it is not writing about this disease.

THE REVIEW REACHES BRAIN ONLY WEAKLY AND SAYS SO. On expression rather than flux: 'The principal component analysis (PCA) of global transcriptome data SUGGESTED that WWOX is involved in maintaining basic glucose metabolism in undifferentiated human neural progenitor cells as well as in differentiated neurons ... Thus, disturbed expression of[WWOX] in nerve cells MOST LIKELY leads to disordered metabolic processes.' And on epilepsy it juxtaposes rather than links: 'WWOX has been also implicated in epilepsy. It was observed that the anaerobic glycolysis and concentration of lactate in the epileptogenic brain increased in comparison to the control ... THE ROLE OF WWOX IN THE CONTROL OF GLUCOSE METABOLISM IN THE CONTEXT OF NEUROLOGICAL DISEASES REQUIRES FURTHER RESEARCH.' That closing sentence is the review's own verdict and should be carried as such.

NO METABOLIC INTERVENTION IS PROPOSED. Verified personally: ketogenic, dichloroacetate and metformin all occur ZERO times (roman-type, informative). The only therapeutic aspiration targets WWOX itself, in diabetes.

THE ARC'S EVIDENTIAL BASE, AS FAR AS PROSE ALLOWS, IS FIVE STRANDS AND TWO ARE THIS GROUP'S OWN: Aqeilan's Wwox-null mouse programme (serum lactate, MEFs, muscle-specific ablation), MCF7 breast cancer cells with a breast-tumour GLUT1 correlation, a Drosophila model, the Lodz group's own gestational-diabetes leukocyte study, and the Lodz group's own 1BR.3.N fibroblast study - which is PMID 35328751 itself. VERDICT: ESSENTIALLY NOTHING TRANSFERS. Cancer DNA-repair biology end to end - no neuron, no brain tissue, no developing CNS, no germline-WWOX patient, no endpoint with a neurodevelopmental analogue. Verified personally: neuron, seizure, epilep*, encephalopath* all ZERO (roman-type, informative); all three 'brain' hits are 'brain cancer'.

THE MOST DISEASE-RELEVANT SENTENCE IN THE PAPER IS A NEGATIVE, AND IT IS IN BODY TEXT SO D-14 DOES NOT SHIELD IT: 'We first considered whether Wwox loss leads to uninduced genome damage (i.e., damage not due to exposure to exogenous cytotoxic agent), but the comet assay ... and immunofluorescence assays for DSB markers, 53BP1 and gammaH2AX, DID NOT REVEAL DIFFERENCES IN UNTREATED Wwox-deficient and -expressing cells.' ABSENT AN EXOGENOUS GENOTOXIN, A WWOX-NULL PRIMARY CELL IS NOT VISIBLY DAMAGED. This LOWERS the prior that WWOX DSB-repair dysregulation drives the neurodevelopmental phenotype.

THE ONE THING THAT DOES TRANSFER IS DOMAIN-RESOLVED AND NARROW: the function characterised here requires an intact WW1 domain and is RETAINED by a WWOX protein carrying the SDR catalytic-site substitution Y293F. Verbatim: 'the SDR mutant Wwox-expressing cells are sensitive to radiation BECAUSE THEY RETAIN A WW1 DOMAIN, which interacts with Brca1.' Binding maps the same way - the WW1 mutant W44F/P47A does not bind Brca1, the WW2 mutant Y85A/P88A does, and a GST-SDR fragment does not.

AND THE CAVEAT ON THAT ITEM IS DECISIVE AND MUST TRAVEL WITH IT. Y293F is a DESIGNED, CONSERVATIVE, CATALYSIS-ABOLISHING substitution chosen to leave the fold intact. A DISEASE MISSENSE IN THE SDR SPAN IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT: it may destabilise or eliminate the protein. THE PAPER MEASURES NO WWOX PROTEIN LEVEL, STABILITY OR LOCALISATION FOR ANY MUTANT, so it cannot distinguish 'SDR catalysis is dispensable' from 'this SDR protein is present and folded'. CITABLE ONLY FOR: SDR catalytic activity is not required for the WWOX-BRCA1 interaction or for WWOX-dependent radiosensitisation. NOTHING BROADER ABOUT SDR MISSENSE ALLELES.

PROTEIN STABILITY: A CLEAN NEGATIVE, verified personally - cycloheximide, half-life, degradation, proteasom*, lysosom* all ZERO (roman-type, informative). THIS PAPER CONTRIBUTES NOTHING to the post-transcriptional-loss question and MUST NOT BE CITED ALONGSIDE the lysosomal-degradation reading of PMID 41124647.

DIRECTION FOR A WWOX-SCARCE GENOTYPE IS ENDPOINT-DEPENDENT AND THE TWO ENDPOINTS OPPOSE: short-term survival of a genotoxin is BETTER with WWOX scarce (knockout MEFs about 10-fold irradiation survival at 7.7 Gy and above; shWWOX MCF10A 25-100-fold bleomycin), via enhanced homology-directed repair and abolished by RAD51 knockdown; genome integrity is WORSE, but mild. evidence_basis: Carvalho C, Correia SC, Seica R, Moreira PI 2022, 'WWOX inhibition by Zfra1-31 restores mitochondrial homeostasis and viability of neuronal cells exposed to high glucose', Cell Mol Life Sci 79(9):487, DOI 10.1007/s00018-022-04508-7. Four authors, ALL University of Coimbra (CNC / CIBB / IIIUC / Institute of Physiology). Chang NS appears ONLY in the reference list (refs 16, 21, 22, 47), never as an author: the GROUP is independent of NCKU, the REAGENT and its specificity claim are not.

PROVENANCE OF THE ARTEFACT. PMC11071800 resolves and returns a zero-length body; no author-manuscript variant exists; this environment has no egress. The operator supplied the publisher PDF on 2026-09-21. PDF sha256 a7ce53cfebfbb879fe3f5a41a63adca3b4d4e9e4a31efbf467668f7d021eeb8f. This deployment has NO PDF toolchain (poppler, PyMuPDF, pypdf all absent; pip install fails at interpreter level), so the text layer was recovered with framework/scripts/pdf_text_extract.py, a stdlib zlib + content-stream extractor written for this read and shipped with 20 tests. The locator here is that tool's --prose view; every count below was produced by `pdf_text_extract.py search` run directly on the PDF, so anyone holding the same PDF reproduces them exactly.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS VALIDATED BEFORE ANY ZERO WAS ACCEPTED, and the tool enforces it: `search` refuses to print a query count until named positive controls come back non-zero. Controls for this read, all live: SH-SY5Y 3, Western blot 35, Zfra1-31 62, WWOX 112, Seahorse 4, Goto-Kakizaki 4, 'loading control' 2, ABN413 1, ab193624 1.

QUESTION 1 OF 2, ANSWERED: NO. There is NO genetic WWOX perturbation of any kind. siRNA 0, shRNA 0, knockdown 0, knockout 0, CRISPR 0, silenc* 0, transfect* 0, lentivir* 0. There is also no specificity control for the peptide: scrambled 0, S8G 0, 'inactive peptide' 0. And no autophagy flux clamp: bafilomycin 0, chloroquine 0, 'autophagic flux' 0. All are TEXT negatives over body, legends, methods and supplementary - D-14 is untouched, no figure-asserted negative is adjudicated from an image here.

A FALSE POSITIVE WAS CAUGHT AND IS THE REASON THE TOOL HAS A BINARY BARRIER. A first, more tolerant matcher returned S8G = 1 for this PDF. Located: the byte run `s\x128G` inside an embedded font program. Replacing non-text runs with a space did NOT fix it - the tolerance bridges a space - so non-text runs are now replaced by an unbridgeable sentinel. Had that hit been taken at face value it would have entered this reading as evidence that the inactive control peptide existed. It does not. Regression-tested.

QUESTION 2 OF 2, ANSWERED - AND THE ANSWER IS ITSELF THE FINDING. The methods antibody table lists BOTH 'Anti-WWOX (phospho Y33) Abcam (ab193624)' AND 'WWOX Merck Millipore (ABN413)' - a TOTAL-WWOX antibody was in hand. NO TOTAL-WWOX RESULT IS REPORTED ANYWHERE: 'total WWOX' 0, 'WWOX expression' 0, and no pWWOX-over-WWOX ratio string occurs in any legend or sentence. All 76 distinct WWOX contexts report pWWOX(tyr33) / 'activated WWOX'. The stated normalisation is verbatim: 'beta-actin was used as a loading control, and bands density was evaluated with the Quantity One Software (Bio-Rad).'

WHY THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT A QUIBBLE: a pTyr33 signal over beta-actin falls if phosphorylation falls OR if WWOX protein falls, and the peptide audit's own section 3.6 finding is that zfration takes WWOX as a SUBSTRATE - i.e. the second reading is the mechanistically expected one. The paper's central pharmacodynamic number, the ~64% reduction, is precisely the quantity that cannot separate 'Zfra inhibited WWOX' from 'Zfra consumed WWOX', and the antibody that would have separated them is listed in its own methods. The title verb 'inhibition' is NOT established by the paper's own data.

WHAT IS GENUINELY SUPPORTED, and it is real evidence: 20 uM Zfra1-31 (Genemed Synthesis, purity >95%), added 3 h (EI) or 24 h (LI) after 25 mM glucose for 48 h, protects differentiated SH-SY5Y cells across a broad, internally coherent panel - viability, membrane potential, Seahorse respirometry, oxidative damage, fission-fusion, MTCO1/ND1/VDAC, autophagy markers, amyloid-beta, pTau, synaptic proteins, p53, caspase-3 - while lowering the pTyr33-WWOX signal. VERBATIM, and note it is the LATE-intervention arm: 'We observed that Zfra1-31 diminished (~64%) the levels of activated WWOX (pWWOX tyr33) (Fig. 3 A) and significantly increased cell viability (~16%; Fig. B).'

THE TEMPORAL CLAIM IS THE PAPER'S BEST-SUPPORTED RESULT: high glucose raised pWWOX(tyr33) ~79% at 24 h (25 mM, maintained at 48 h) and ~60% at 10 mM (significant only at 48 h), while viability fell only ~15% and only at 48 h. WWOX activation PRECEDES the damage. That does not require the causal attribution and survives it.

THE ANIMAL ARM IS BETTER CONTROLLED THAN THE ABSTRACT SUGGESTS, AND IT IS NON-MONOTONIC. Verbatim: 'young animals (6-month-old) present increased levels of pWWOX (tyr33), when compared to AGE-MATCHED CONTROL RATS and to 12-month-old GK rats' - cortex ~+20%, hippocampus ~two-fold. But at 12 months the cortical signal FALLS ~20% and the hippocampal difference is not significant. NO ANIMAL RECEIVED ZFRA: the GK arm is purely observational and tests nothing about intervention.

THE ONLY GENETIC WWOX RESULT IN THE PAPER BELONGS TO SOMEONE ELSE AND MUST NOT BE RE-VOICED AS A9's. Verbatim: 'it was previously shown that inhibition of tyr33 phosphorylation by a dominant-negative WWOX was able to abolish apoptotic cell death in a MPP+ rat model for PD' - reference [18], i.e. the MPP+ line already held as PMID 18371080 / FT-109. Under D-15 a secondary source's attribution is not evidence for the attributed result.

THE PEPTIDE-SPECIFICITY CONTROL THE PAPER RELIES ON IS NOT SHOWN. Verbatim: 'Zfra1-31, besides being effective against high glucose-induced mitochondrial defects, does not affect mitochondria and cells function under control conditions (DATA NOT SHOWN).' With no scrambled peptide and no total WWOX, the paper contains NO shown control separating a WWOX-mediated effect of Zfra1-31 from any other effect of a 20 uM covalent peptide.

THE AUTHORS' OWN LIMITATION, recorded because it travels with any use of the animal arm: 'Due to the limited amount of rat brain samples, we were unable to perform key experiments done in neuronal cells.'

CANONICAL FORMULATION, to travel wherever this paper is cited in this repository: Independent neuronal evidence that Zfra1-31 is protective while reducing the pY33-WWOX signal. Causal attribution of that protection to WWOX INHIBITION remains unresolved - no orthogonal genetic WWOX perturbation was performed, no inactive-peptide control is shown, and total WWOX was never measured, so the reduction in pY33 signal is not separable from a reduction in WWOX protein.

EFFECT ON THE REPOSITORY: no new CLAIM. The 2026-09-20 peptide-audit addendum sentence 'an independent lab confirms that INHIBITING WWOX is protective in neurons' is narrowed to 'an independent lab confirms that Zfra1-31 is protective in neurons and lowers pY33-WWOX'. The audit's therapeutic conclusion for the reference genotype is UNCHANGED and if anything firmer: inhibition and consumption point the same way in a genotype whose problem is too little functional WWOX, so it remains a category objection, not a dosing one. HYP-20260705-05 keeps its status - this read shows the paper does not test its falsifiable statement.

REVIVAL_TRIGGER: any publication reporting TOTAL WWOX protein alongside pTyr33-WWOX under Zfra1-31, or any genetic WWOX arm beside the peptide in a neuronal model, reopens this - that single measurement decides between the two readings above.

evidence_basis: EVIDENCE TIER: PREPRINT, NOT PEER REVIEWED. bioRxiv, posted 2025-01-18, DOI 10.1101/2025.01.17.633677. PMID 39868255 and PMC11761808 exist but index the preprint, not a peer-reviewed article. No tier promotion is taken from the presence of a PMID.

Identity verified from the PDF and from PubMed metadata, which agree: De La Cruz P, Gomes M, Lockett A, Fisher A, Cook T, Smith P, Lloyd C, Twigg HL III, Oblak A, Aldaz CM, Machado RF. Aldaz and Machado are co-senior authors; Aldaz supplied the mouse line.

MODEL, and this is the load-bearing scope limit: the challenged animals are HETEROZYGOUS Wwox WT/P47T versus WT/WT littermates. n = 6 male + 3 female per group, mean age 2.6 months, single 10 mg/kg intraperitoneal LPS dose, euthanised at 12 hours. P47T is a SCAR12-class allele that impairs WW-domain protein-protein interaction; it is not a WOREE null allele.

The paper's own framing confines the result to challenge: 'our results contribute to prior studies demonstrating Wwox WT/P47T mice do not differ significantly from Wwox WT/WT littermates at baseline. However, when challenged with experimental sepsis, the Wwox WT/P47T mice demonstrate a more severe phenotype.' This is a gene-environment interaction result, not a baseline disease model.

Endpoints verified verbatim. Sickness behaviour: reduced distance travelled post-LPS in BOTH genotypes (p<0.0001), so that endpoint is not genotype-specific; reduced time in centre in WT/P47T (p=0.0312) and not in WT/WT, which is a within-genotype comparison rather than a genotype-by-treatment interaction test. Sepsis severity: WT/P47T LPS worse than WT/WT LPS (p=0.001617).

Gliosis verified: Iba1 microglia density WT/P47T LPS > WT/WT LPS in frontal cortex (p=0.0282) and hippocampus (p=0.0490). GFAP astrocyte density WT/P47T LPS > WT/WT LPS in cortex (p=0.0005), and within WT/P47T LPS vs its own PBS (p=0.0040). 'There was no difference in astrocyte density in the hippocampus between groups.' The regional dissociation reported in the operator brief is confirmed exactly.

Apoptosis verified, and the authors bound it themselves: 'There was no difference in area of CC3 or the percent of neurons positive for CC3 in the cortex in response to LPS. In the hippocampus, there was an increase in area of CC3+ immunostaining in the Wwox WT/P47T LPS group compared to the Wwox WT/WT LPS group (p=0.0226) but no difference in CC3-positive neurons. This suggests a regional difference in susceptibility to LPS between genotypes that is not affecting neurons.' The affected apoptotic cell type is explicitly unresolved.

CORRECTION to the preliminary read, which listed 'inflammatory response' as uniformly greater. The peripheral picture is DISCORDANT, not amplified: 'Plasma IL-6 levels were significantly elevated in Wwox WT/WT LPS mice compared to PBS control (p=0.0168) with no difference in the Wwox WT/P47T mice. Plasma TNF- levels were elevated in the Wwox WT/WT LPS mice (p=0.0025) with no difference in the Wwox WT/P47T groups.' The greater response holds for CORTICAL mRNA (IL-6, TNF-alpha) and NOT for plasma protein. The abstract's blanket 'increase in inflammatory response' oversells the plasma data.

Limitations, the authors' own: no time course, blood-brain-barrier permeability not examined, signalling pathways out of scope, and 'the possibility of baseline inflammation observed in the Wwox WT/P47T mice'. Added by this reading: n=9 per group, one 12-hour timepoint, and no multiple-comparison correction across the reported endpoints, which bears on the hippocampal microglia value at p=0.0490.

Transfer scope recorded at read time: this does NOT transfer to WOREE null disease, to chronic neurodegeneration, or to any therapeutic efficacy claim. It is a modifier / stress-sensitivity lead at preprint tier, and no therapeutic node is promoted from it.

PMC reader HTML, 184,333 bytes, carrying the whole body; screened for zero C0 controls with the operators PRESENT ('<' x17, '+/-' x26, 'x' x3, 'beta' x14, 14 P< or P= hits), so it does not trip suspicion by absence and every text locator is verified against it. Route facts, measured: Europe PMC fullTextXML 404/0 bytes; efetch db=pmc 14,992 bytes of front matter with the publisher's explicit XML refusal, no <body>, and a single <fig> that is the graphical abstract; THERE IS NO PDF AT PMC FOR THIS ARTICLE AT ALL - pmc_pow_fetch 404 and ?pdf=render 404 'No PDF file found for pmcid: PMC11380939', so the proof-of-work route that won on PMID 33058734 does not exist here. The winning routes were the PMC reader HTML under NO User-Agent (200 here, where the same policy returned a reCAPTCHA on the companion paper) and the PMC blob CDN reached through the article page's own src attributes.

SUPPLEMENTS EXIST AND THE METADATA FLAG IS WRONG. Europe PMC reports hasSuppl=N; the article's own SUPPLEMENTAL DATA section names Supplemental Table S1 and Supplemental Fig. S1 at doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.25137089. Both retrieved from figshare article 25137089 (CC BY 4.0), fingerprinted, and inspected. Europe PMC supplementaryFiles returned 'Article with id PMC11380939 is not open access one', a licence refusal that says nothing about existence and is the easy thing to misread as absence. Both are load-bearing: Supplemental Fig. S1 is the endothelial-restriction control, Supplemental Table S1 is the 2,051-protein table behind the zyxin and SOD2 claims.

figures: 8 of 8 main figures, all panels, inspected as images, plus Supplemental Fig. S1 and the ZYX and SOD2 rows of the 42-page Supplemental Table S1 read at source. CEILING DECLARED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATE: the main figures are PMC derivative rasters 770-836 px wide (the graphical abstract is 667x500, the size class of this repository's 2026-09-09 near-error) and no PDF exists at PMC to render anything crisper from, so where a fine judgement rested on that raster it is reported as such. The supplement is vector and was rendered at 300 dpi.

WHAT THE READING ESTABLISHES: zyxin up at protein and mRNA (Supplemental Table S1 row 2051, BH-adj P 0.0001, log2FC +0.55 = about 1.46-fold, verified at source and only just past the +/-0.5 fold-change line), SOD2 down (log2FC -0.94, the larger effect, unpursued); WWOX silencing roughly doubles stretch-induced IL-6 and IL-8 in human ECs by ELISA; the MAPK change is DIRECTIONALLY SPLIT with ERK and JNK up but p38 DOWN; EC Wwox KO mice sustain worse VILI at n=10 per group; and BAL IL-6, KC, IL-1beta and MCP-1 are ALL significantly higher - inflammation is the positive measured endpoint here.

THE STRONGEST RESULT IS AN INTERVENTION AND IT IS SELECTIVE: dual silencing of WWOX and zyxin cut stretch-induced IL-8 by 35% while leaving IL-6 unchanged (Fig 7E, the WWOX-versus-dual comparison marked ns). Zyxin is therefore a specific mediator of the IL-8 limb and not a general inflammatory switch. n=3 transfections - the paper's most important result rests on its smallest n.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: no zyxin manipulation in any mouse, so the mechanistic intervention is in vitro only; the WWOX-to-zyxin mechanism is left as two untested alternatives plus a SMAD3 hypothesis assembled from two OTHER papers; the authors themselves declare the nuclear-translocation limit (no fractionation, no confocal z-stacking) and the endpoint is a blinded VISUAL colocalisation score; and THERE IS NO ECIS/TER AND NO TRANSWELL ASSAY ANYWHERE IN THIS PAPER - the companion paper's barrier assays are dropped, 'barrier' is represented only by BAL protein in vivo, and the paper's own verb for the leak-cytokine relation is 'correlated'.

tables: not_present is a measurement - the article prints no main-text table; Supplemental Table S1 is supplementary and is covered there. limitations: not_present as a SECTION, with limitation content inside the Discussion including one explicit author-declared limit.

references: 33 enumerated from the PMC reader anchors (range 1-33, no gaps). Gene-direct and load-bearing references resolved by command in this session, never from recall; TWO WOULD NOT RESOLVE and their identifiers are left NULL rather than guessed - reference 2 (Hussain 2019) and reference 31 (Ferguson/Aldaz 2013, the WWOX-SMAD3 paper the Discussion leans on) - and reference 16's title returned 2 hits so its identifier is flagged as needing confirmation.

retraction_check: no notice on this PMID and the three routes AGREE here, unlike on the companion paper - Europe PMC returns only 'Preprint in' PPR685537, ESummary returns empty in JSON and no block in XML with none of Retract/Erratum/Expression of Concern in 3,032 bytes. corrected_items declared empty by fact. retraction_check.dependencies: SCREENED_CLEAN over 33 of 33 references, all 33 carrying a DOI, zero unscreenable and zero flagged.

AN INTEGRITY FINDING THE TOOL DID NOT PRODUCE, FOUND BY READING THE REFERENCE LIST: reference 15, PMID 20705921 (Wojtowicz 2010, Circ Res), CARRIES AN ERRATUM - Circ Res 2010;107(9):e15-6 - printed in this article's own reference list and confirmed independently through Europe PMC. That paper is the SOLE source for zyxin's function as a stretch-induced IL-8 enhancer, i.e. the reason zyxin was selected from the proteomic screen at all. Its scope is unknown to me because I did not retrieve it, so this is a prompt to read and never a claim about either paper. An erratum is not a retraction.

SELF-CORRECTIONS MADE DURING THIS READING: three `qualifies` pointers I wrote were SELF-REFERENTIAL and the validator refused them ('a locator cannot qualify itself'); they are withdrawn rather than re-pointed, because an assertion about another locator belongs to the evidence that makes it, and for the p38 case that assertion already sits correctly on the Fig 3 panel entry. Three snippets fell below the 30-character floor and were replaced with the drawn row and label text in full.

FIELD DENSITY, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING: zyxin has 26 records with stretch or ventilation and exactly 1 with WWOX, which is this paper. WWOX and VILI is 1 record; WWOX and mechanotransduction is 1; WWOX and SOD2 is 1. Each of this paper's three mechanistic novelties is a literature of one paper, itself, against 136 records for WWOX and brain out of 708 WWOX records.

The 'more favourable DFS group' column CONFIRMS the running-text directions for all five subtypes.

SOURCE-INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN TABLE S7: no single HR orientation reconciles the HR column with the 'more favourable DFS group' column. Under the caption's 'High vs Low', basal-like (1.11, 'high'), Lum A (0.46, 'low') and OV (0.96, 'low') disagree; under the reverse orientation HER2-enriched (0.17, 'high') and Lum B (1.32, 'low') disagree. Supplementary Figure S1 (image-inspected; INFERENZA from curve geometry, not a printed value) fits the reverse orientation — Lum A low-ratio curve stays ~0.92 while high falls to ~0.74 with HR = 0.46 printed — and shows the HER2 high-ratio curve dropping to 0 near t≈1650 while low holds ~0.93 to t≈3050, and the Luminal B low-ratio curve ending at 0. The HER2-enriched and Luminal B labels, and the body's downstream pathway framing built on them, are therefore contested by the source's own numbers.

TABLE S6 (pp.6–7) CONFIRMS the body's continuous-ratio Cox values verbatim: Breast ratio only 0.25 (0.15–0.44), 5.7 × 10⁻⁷, concordance 0.66; Breast WWOX+HIF1A+ratio: ratio 0.31 (0.14–0.70), 4.8 × 10⁻³, WWOX 0.74 and HIF1A 0.43 n.s.; Ovarian ratio only 1.11 (0.92–1.35), 0.27, 0.49; Ovarian combined ratio 1.44 (0.99–2.09), 0.055, 0.55. The ratio is 'a standardized continuous covariate (per standard deviation increase)': higher ratio = lower hazard in BRCA (significant), point estimate >1 in OV (n.s./borderline). Sign non-invariance holds at table level.

TABLES S4–S5 (p.5) are the LASSO-selected multivariable Cox models (BRCA N=390, 22 events; OV N=228, 161 events) and contain NO WWOX, HIF1A or ratio row, although Methods states the penalized model 'incorporated ... and the WWOX/HIF1A ratio'. TABLE S8 (pp.8–9) is a DEG × ESR1/ESR2/AR target-gene intersection list per subtype; it carries no survival direction.

No panel of that figure contains a neuron; the in-neuron work in this paper is binding - FRET in primary DRG cultures, immuno-EM in tissue - never transcriptional output.

THE CHRONIC RESULT IS NOT LATERALISED. The Results sentence places the month-2 co-activation in both the non-injured and the injured side, and Supplementary Figure S3 gives the numbers: contralateral small neurons about 72 percent with nuclear p-WOX1 at month 2 against about 71 percent ipsilaterally, with sham animals already at about 37 percent contralateral and 31 percent ipsilateral. Axotomy is therefore not the sufficient cause of the chronic phase the title names.

THE HEADLINE PERCENTAGES ARE BIN LABELS. Figure 4, which carries the whole time course, is a categorical heat map with five ordinal bins (none 0%, very low under 20%, low 20-40%, moderate 40-65%, high over 65%) and no n, no error and no test anywhere on it. The abstract's 'greater than 65%' and '40-65%' are those bins.

The death the title calls a delayed loss is 'less than 5% neuronal death' at the two-month endpoint; the larger 37-percent-by-week-32 figure the Discussion leans on is another laboratory's. Two Discussion steps - WOX1 binding IkB-alpha and the nuclear NF-kB consequence - are attributed to unpublished data of the same laboratory.

FIGURE 5a ADJUDICATES THE PAPER'S INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: Results say the Y112F mutant aggregates less and the Discussion says it does not; the panel reports p = 0.844 (TPC6A-delta), p = 0.040 (Y112F) and p = 0.002 (S35G) for medium versus TGF-beta1, so the mutant the Results call non-aggregating has the most significant TGF-beta1 response. evidence_basis: FT-104 IS DISCHARGED, AND THE OUTCOME IS WORSE THAN THE FLAG IT PROTECTED. Supplementary Figure 1, now extracted and rendered, is the paper's only WWOX-genotype datum and its numbers do not reproduce its own legend. The legend claims a memory drop 'greater than 55%' at ages 10-12 in Wwox+/- against under 50% in 3xTg. The figure's x-axes read 3, >10, 8, 10 months, carry NO genotype label on any bar, contain no age 12, and have no n per bar, no error convention and no statistical test; under either assignment of the two bar pairs to the two genotypes the drops are about 43%/13% (short-term) and about 52%/33% (long-term). No arrangement yields 'greater than 55 percent'.

IT IS NOT A WWOX MODEL. The treated animals are 3xTg-AD (Psen1 M146V, APPswe, tau P301L) with wild-type Wwox; there is no WWOX allele in the intervention cohort. WWOX enters only as the pS14-WWOX phospho-epitope in a melanoma model in nude mice, and as the supplementary panel above.

DOSE, ROUTE, SCHEDULE, CONTROLS: Zfra4-10 at 2 mM in 100 microlitres of PBS by tail vein, four consecutive weekly injections from 10 months of age, PBS sham as the only comparator - no vehicle-plus-scrambled-peptide arm, no dose-response, no pharmacokinetics. The melanoma arm of the same paper uses 1 mM in sterile water, a different dose and vehicle for the same peptide.
BLINDING AND RANDOMISATION ARE NOT MENTIONED: 'blind' and 'randomi' occur 0 times in the fingerprinted artefact.

GROUP SIZES ARE INCONSISTENT FOUR WAYS for one cohort: Methods five Zfra and five sham; Figure 1A PBS n = 6 and Zfra n = 5; Figure 1B PBS n = 12 and Zfra n = 10; Figure 2 PBS n = 3 and Zfra n = 5. The histology statistics are computed over fields (Fig 3C, n = 10) and cells (Fig 3D, n = 40), not animals - pseudoreplication in a cohort of at most ten mice.

THE FINDING OF THIS READING: the sentence 'WWOX binds Tau via its C-terminal SDR domain' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the fingerprinted artefact, inside the abstract, and ZERO times in the body. THREE SENTENCES CARRIED AS RESTATEMENTS, NOT MEASUREMENTS: (1) 'it only takes less than 15 days after birth' is a ceiling imposed by the null mouse's one-month lifespan, not a measured latency, and is juvenile rather than embryonic - the cascade has no embryonic datum at any node. (3) 'the stronger the binding strength ... the better the extent of cancer suppression', carried into a therapeutic recommendation in section 10.3, is an analogy transferred from cancer with no neuronal measurement.

TABLE 1, now read, contains four proposals and no results; its second row expects combined Zfra-plus-WWOX peptides 'to block seizure associated with WWOX deficiency-related syndromes such as WOREE in newborns'. That is the only place in this group where the therapeutic programme is pointed at a WWOX-DEE phenotype at all, and it rests on no data.

The selection called this 'the window lesson'. The paper does not claim a closed developmental window: it attributes the P10 failure to transgene level and distribution, supports that with its own IHC showing substantially restricted expression after P10 dosing, and notes that single-stranded AAV needs 7-14 days to reach therapeutic levels so expression would have arrived after seizure onset at P10-13. The answer to the question the selection posed is dose and biodistribution, not window.

Doses, verbatim from Methods: 1 uL per hemisphere at P2 giving 1.1e11 to 1.7e11 vector genomes per mouse, and 2 uL per hemisphere at P10 giving 2.2e11 to 3.4e11. The Results text calls the P10 dose 3.4e11, 'twice the dose'; the Methods give the range. Vector titres 5.3e13 to 8.5e13 genome copies per mL.

Table 1, read from the image: three untreated and three treated null mice, scored on three days each; untreated average 16.4 events/day under 10 s and 8.7 over 10 s, treated 8 and 0. No statistical test, confidence interval or p value appears in the table. The headline seizure endpoint is n = 3 per arm, video-scored, with no electrographic confirmation, and the authors say so.

Overexpression in wild-type brain is not neutral at the cellular level: treated WT PV+ interneurons showed a leftward, hyperpolarizing shift in the input-output curve. The organism-level 'no obvious adverse effects' is an absence-of-evidence statement, and body weight was never rescued in treated nulls.

evidence_basis: The whole Main text, the Methods and the legends of Figures 1-2 and Extended Data Figs. 1-7 read from the JATS XML. Panels were not inspected and the Supplementary Information (Supplementary Figs. 1-4, Tables 1-3) was acquired but not opened. PubMed article types: Journal Article, Case Reports; no retraction, correction or expression of concern.
No WWOX content. Public edition: described at the level of allele class, route and schedule only.

The exposure record does not agree with itself, and the schedule is the parameter a reader would transfer: the abstract says 19 intrathecal administrations over 20 months; the Main text accounts for seven doses totalling 30.5 mg plus ten further doses of 8 mg, which is seventeen administrations and about 110.5 mg; the Extended Data Fig. 5 caption says 94 mg in total until the age of 21 months. What is consistent and usable is the interval: 4 to 6 weeks, derived from measured CSF concentrations and a modelled cortical profile rather than from convention.

The mechanism does not transfer to a loss-of-function disease: this is a gapmer that degrades mRNA in a gain-of-function channelopathy, and the paper itself notes SCN2A is intolerant of both haploinsufficiency and dosage increase. What transfers is architectural: mechanism confirmation by voltage clamp before dosing, the intrathecal route with a defined infant safety panel, a PK-derived redosing interval, and the expanded-access pathway.

The honest warning this case carries: status epilepticus was broken and seizure frequency fell by more than 60 percent, while neurodevelopment did not improve and serial MRI showed progressive cortical atrophy attributed to the disease. Seizure reduction is not a proxy for developmental outcome, and the authors say the question is open.

What is weaker than the abstract: the uORF result is a transfected plasmid reporter in HEK-293, and the authors' own ASOs against those uAUGs failed to raise luciferase. The dynamic range is not quantified and is admitted to need optimisation; every HiBiT assay came from a single plating of cells; the upregulating ASO is proprietary; and the chosen clone carries a 985-kb 20q11.21 duplication including BCL2L1.

Transfer limits stated in the dossier: nothing here is WWOX-specific, C-terminal tagging tolerance for WWOX is untested, a HiBiT readout reports abundance and not oxidoreductase activity, and the line's own caveats travel with the method and should be designed out rather than inherited.

evidence_basis: Candidate-SNP association study, 864 normolipidaemic versus 1129 dyslipidaemic adults of one ethnic minority population; nothing is perturbed, no WWOX transcript or protein is measured, and the authors list functional work among their own limitations.

The two SNPs assigned to WWOX are about 500 kb apart and in weak linkage disequilibrium with each other, stated by the authors; a haplotype across that distance is not a statement about one WWOX allele. The positions the paper prints (78058601 and 78624496) also place rs2222896 outside the WWOX gene body as given in the same genome build by the other human source of this wave (chr16:78133551-79246564), roughly 75 kb 5-prime of the gene.

The authors themselves withdraw the WWOX-intronic association that motivated the study: rs2548861 fails to replicate against HDL-C in the normal group (P = 0.597) and they conclude that 'mutations at rs2548861 were not correlated with HDL-C concentration in these subjects'.
Only SNPs with minor allele frequency above 10 percent were eligible, so nothing here bears on a rare damaging WWOX allele or on any carrier of one.

Two internal inconsistencies recorded: the abstract gives the rs3132584 x rs2222896 interaction as increasing dyslipidaemia risk 2.548-fold 'and predicted hypertension' while the Results give 1.523-fold for hypertension; and Table 1 prints the normal group's weight as 54.48 plus-minus 110.29 kg.

Multiplicity priced rather than ignored: fourteen GMDR-selected 'optimal' interaction models over four SNPs plus environment are reported from the same dataset as the primary tests, and one haplotype-disease odds ratio is 15.08 (95% CI 9.24-24.60) beside per-genotype odds ratios below 3.

evidence_basis: What this pass adds to the standing receipt is the SECOND ARM, which no LEGEND record mentions: lentiviral WWOX cDNA overexpression at about 850-fold mRNA and more than 700-fold protein, run across the same four crossed oxygen and glucose conditions as the knockdown.

THE DOSE-RESPONSE IS NOT MONOTONE ON THE ENDPOINT THE CORPUS WOULD MOST WANT TO USE. Medium lactate rises under WWOX depletion in all four conditions, and it ALSO rises under WWOX overexpression relative to wild type in normoxia-normoglycaemia and in hypoxia-hyperglycaemia. A lactate readout therefore cannot be specified as a monotone reporter of WWOX dose in this system.

Glucose uptake reverses sign with condition in BOTH arms: depletion raises uptake in normoxia-normoglycaemia and lowers it in hypoxia-hyperglycaemia; overexpression raises it in normoxia-hyperglycaemia and lowers it in hypoxia.

The loss-of-function arm is a partial depletion the paper calls KO throughout: about three-fold lower mRNA and about 8.5-fold lower protein in a puromycin-selected polyclonal population. Any statement inheriting the word knockout from this paper inherits a knockdown.

The oxidative arm was measured and was null: citrate synthase expression and activity show no WWOX influence in any condition, and pyruvate dehydrogenase activity is unchanged under depletion. No respirometry of any kind is performed.

TWO ASSAYS OF HIF1-ALPHA PROTEIN DISAGREE INSIDE THE PAPER AND ONLY ONE REACHES THE DISCUSSION. The Discussion asserts increased protein 'together with its translocation to the nucleus'; the fractionated immunoblot reports the protein significantly DECREASED in the cytoplasm of the depleted cells in two conditions and states 'We didn't observed WWOX influence on HIF1alpha protein in nuclear fraction'. Whole-cell immunocytochemistry does show an increase in the two normoxic conditions. The robust positive of the paper is the HRE transactivation reporter, not the protein level and not the translocation.

The system is ONE immortalised human skin fibroblast line (1BR.3.N, ECACC 90020508). Nothing neural and nothing developmental is measured, and no metabolic intervention is proposed or evaluated; the paper's only therapeutic sentence targets WWOX itself in diabetes.
